title: Topic 11 · Status Games vs. Wealth Creation

sents.t: Satisfaction games, the allure of accruing, whether it’s fame, actual fame, or just the competition comparison trap, it’s always there.
sents.zh: 满足感的游戏、积累的诱惑，不管是名气、真正的名气，还是单纯的竞争攀比陷阱，它一直都在。
gloss: 心里被填满的那种“够了”
把两样东西放天平两边。

sents.t: There’s a real draw of being swayed by social approval, but how should people learn to get less distracted by status games in that way?
sents.zh: 被社会认可左右是很有吸引力的，但人们该怎样学会少被这种地位游戏分心呢？
gloss: 眼睛被别的东西勾走了。

sents.t: I think it just helps to see that status games don’t matter as much as they used to.
sents.zh: 我觉得，看清地位游戏已经不像过去那么重要，会很有帮助。

sents.t: In old society, let’s go back to hunter-gatherer times, there was no such thing as wealth – you just had what you could carry.
sents.zh: 在古代社会，我们回到狩猎采集时代，那时根本没有财富这种东西——你只有自己能带走的东西。
gloss: 拿弓打猎、伸手摘果的原始人。

sents.t: There was no stored wealth, so wealth creation games didn’t exist.
sents.zh: 没有可以储存的财富，所以创造财富的游戏并不存在。

sents.t: All that existed was status games.
sents.zh: 存在的只有地位游戏。

sents.t: If you were high status, then you got what little was available first, but even back then you had to earn your status by taking care of the tribe.
sents.zh: 如果你地位高，就能先拿到那一点点可用的东西，但即使在那时，你也得靠照顾部落来赢得地位。

sents.t: Now we have wealth creation where you can actually create a product or a service.
sents.zh: 现在我们有了财富创造，你真的可以创造一个产品或一项服务。

sents.t: You can scale that product or service and you can provide abundance for a lot of people, and that’s not zero-sum, that’s a positive-sum game.
sents.zh: 你可以把那个产品或服务做大，为很多人提供充裕的东西，这不是零和，而是正和游戏。

sents.t: I can be wealthy, you can be wealthy, we can create things together.
sents.zh: 我可以富有，你也可以富有，我们可以一起创造东西。

sents.t: And clearly since we are all collectively far, far wealthier than we were in hunter-gatherer times, wealth creation is positive.
sents.zh: 很明显，既然我们整体上比狩猎采集时代富裕得多得多，财富创造就是正面的。

sents.t: But status is limited.
sents.zh: 但地位是有限的。

sents.t: There’s limited status to go around.
sents.zh: 地位就那么多，不够大家分。

sents.t: It’s a ranking ladder, it’s a hierarchy, and so if one person rises in status, somebody else has to lower in status.
sents.zh: 它是一个排名的梯子，是一种等级制度，所以如果一个人地位上升，就得有别人地位下降。
gloss: 一级一级往上爬的梯子。

sents.t: Now you can have multiple kinds of status, so you can expand some kinds of status,
sents.zh: 当然，地位可以有很多种，所以有些种类的地位可以扩大，

sents.t: but it’s not like wealth creation where it can go infinitely, where we can all be living in the stars and moon bases or Mars colonies.
sents.zh: 但它不像财富创造那样可以无限增长，让我们都住到星空里、月球基地或火星殖民地去。

sents.t: Just realize the status games are inherently limited.
sents.zh: 只要意识到，地位游戏天生就是有限的。

sents.t: They’re always combative.
sents.zh: 它们总是带着对抗性。

sents.t: They always require direct combat, whereas wealth creation games can be just you creating products – you don’t have to fight anybody else.
sents.zh: 它们总需要直接对抗，而财富创造的游戏可以只是你在做产品——你不用和任何人斗。

sents.t: Yes, in the marketplace your product has to succeed,
sents.zh: 没错，在市场上你的产品必须成功，

sents.t: but that’s not quite the same as invective against other people or being angry with other people or feeling pushed down or pushed up or having a beef with somebody.
sents.zh: 但这和谩骂攻击别人、生别人的气、觉得被打压或被抬高、或者和谁结梁子，并不完全一样。

sents.t: So I would argue that wealth creation games are both more pleasant, they’re positive-sum, and they actually have concrete material returns.
sents.zh: 所以我认为，财富创造的游戏更愉快，它们是正和的，而且真的有实实在在的物质回报。
gloss: 摆出理由说：我认为是这样
像水泥一样实实在在、摸得到。
付出之后回到你手里的东西。

sents.t: If you have more money, you can buy more.
sents.zh: 钱多了，你就能买更多。

sents.t: Show me where you can exchange your status at the bank.
sents.zh: 你倒是告诉我，在哪家银行能把地位换成钱。
gloss: 你给我这个，我给你那个。

sents.t: Exactly, it’s vague and fuzzy.
sents.zh: 没错，它模糊又说不清。

sents.t: Now, you see people get rich, they have money, what do they want?
sents.zh: 你看，人们变富了，有钱了，他们想要什么？

sents.t: They want status, so they go to Hollywood, start starring in movies, they donate to non-profits, they go to Cannes or Davos, and they start trying to trade the money for status.
sents.zh: 他们想要地位，于是去好莱坞、开始主演电影，给非营利组织捐款，去戛纳或达沃斯，开始试着用钱换地位。
gloss: 站在电影海报的正中间。
不为赚钱、只为帮人的组织。

sents.t: People always want what they don’t have, and we are evolutionarily hardwired for status because as I said, wealth creation didn’t really exist until the agricultural revolution when you could store grain.
sents.zh: 人总是想要自己没有的东西，而我们在进化上天生就渴望地位，因为正如我说的，直到农业革命、人们能储存粮食之后，财富创造才真正出现。
gloss: 从猴子到人的漫长路上形成的。
线路焊死在里面，改不了。
人类开始种地的大转变。

sents.t: Then the industrial revolution took it to another level and now the information age is taking it to yet another level.
sents.zh: 后来工业革命把它提升到了另一个层次，现在信息时代又把它推向了更高的层次。
gloss: 把它提升到另一个层次
人人手里拿着网络的时代。

sents.t: There’s never been an easier time to make money.
sents.zh: 赚钱从来没有像现在这么容易过。

sents.t: Yes, it’s still hard, but there’s never been an easier time to create wealth, because there’s so much leverage out there, there’s so much opportunity.
sents.zh: 没错，赚钱还是很难，但创造财富从来没有这么容易过，因为外面有那么多杠杆、那么多机会。
gloss: 一根撬棍，小力气撬大石头。

sents.t: You still have to go find it, it’s not easy, it’s not gonna fall on your lap and you have to learn something and know something and do something interesting,
sents.zh: 你还是得自己去找，这不容易，机会不会自己掉到你怀里，你得学点东西、懂点东西、做点有意思的事，

sents.t: but nevertheless it’s possible to many more people.
sents.zh: 但尽管如此，现在对多得多的人来说，这都是可能的。

sents.t: A few hundred years ago you were born a serf, you were gonna die a serf, there was almost no way out of that.
sents.zh: 几百年前，你生来是农奴，死的时候也还是农奴，几乎没有出路。
gloss: 一辈子给地主种地的人。

sents.t: That’s changed, and so I would argue that you’re better off focusing on wealth games than status games.
sents.zh: 这已经变了，所以我认为，你专注于财富游戏比专注于地位游戏更好。

sents.t: If you’re trying to build up, for example, your following on a social network and get famous and then get rich off of being famous,
sents.zh: 比如说，如果你想在社交网络上积累粉丝，先出名，再靠名气发财，

sents.t: that’s a much harder path than getting rich first, and then go for your fame afterwards would be my advice.
sents.zh: 那条路比先变富、之后再去追求名气要难得多，这是我的建议。
gloss: 把经验递给别人，告诉他怎么做更好

sents.t: A lot of people do that, as you said.
sents.zh: 正如你说的，很多人都这么做。

sents.t: It’s funny how people who have achieved such a level of wealth – you think why do you need the status, given that most people use status to then try and cash in to achieve wealth?
sents.zh: 有意思的是，那些已经达到这种财富水平的人——你会想，你为什么还需要地位？毕竟大多数人是用地位去变现、去获得财富的。
gloss: 把这个事实摆在桌上考虑。

sents.t: If you’ve achieved “fuck you money” already, if you’re post-money or asset-heavy as it’s known, why are you trying to go in the other direction?
sents.zh: 如果你已经有了“可以对谁都说不的钱”，如果你已经不再为钱发愁、或者说资产雄厚，你为什么还要往反方向走？
gloss: 多到可以对谁都说不的钱（粗口）。
手里压着很多房子和股票。

sents.t: As you said, because we’ve got an illustrious history biologically of wanting status, and wealth is kind of novel.
sents.zh: 正如你说的，因为从生物学上讲，我们追求地位有着悠久“辉煌”的历史，而财富算是新鲜事物。

sents.t: It’s new.
sents.zh: 它是新的。

sents.t: Wealth is something that you have to understand more intellectually.
sents.zh: 财富是你需要更多用头脑去理解的东西。

sents.t: Yeah, there’s a physical component, more food, more survival,
sents.zh: 是的，它有物质层面的部分，更多食物、更容易生存，

sents.t: but to truly understand the effects and the powers and the abilities and limitations, and the advantages and disadvantages of wealth, you have to use your neocortex a lot more.
sents.zh: 但要真正理解财富的影响、力量、能力和局限，以及它的好处和坏处，你得更多地动用你的大脑新皮层。
gloss: 大脑最外层、负责思考的那一圈。

sents.t: Does that mean the reason to play the game is to win the game and be done with it?
sents.zh: 那是不是说，玩这个游戏的理由就是赢下它，然后就此了结？
gloss: 玩这个游戏；按规则参与

sents.t: Is it harder to win and be done with for status than it is for wealth?
sents.zh: 地位是不是比财富更难赢下、更难了结？

sents.t: That’s a good observation, I hadn’t thought that through, but you’re right.
sents.zh: 这个观察很到位，我之前没想透，但你说得对。

sents.t: I think people will always want more status, but I think you can be satisfied at a certain level of wealth.
sents.zh: 我觉得人们永远会想要更多地位，但财富到了一定程度，你是可以满足的。

sents.t: Well, you always have this sort of sense, and this is what leaderboards are.
sents.zh: 嗯，你总会有这种感觉，这就是排行榜的本质。
gloss: 谁领先一目了然的榜单。

sents.t: That’s right.
sents.zh: 没错。

sents.t: And it is zero-sum.
sents.zh: 而且它是零和的。

sents.t: And it is, I guess, you know, the Forbes richest people on the planet.
sents.zh: 我想也就是，你知道的，福布斯全球富豪榜那种。

sents.t: Yeah.
sents.zh: 对。

sents.t: That one’s harder to climb the ladder on,
sents.zh: 那个榜单上的梯子更难爬，

sents.t: but the fact that, for example, iTunes and YouTube can put you in competition against your contemporaries every single day, and make you go up and down and show you likes and comments and ratings.
sents.zh: 但事实是，比如 iTunes 和 YouTube 每天都能让你和同时代的人竞争，让你的排名上上下下，给你看点赞、评论和评分。

sents.t: This is how much you fell, this is how much you’re up.
sents.zh: 你掉了多少名，你又涨了多少名。

sents.t: Exactly.
sents.zh: 没错。

sents.t: They’ll keep you running on that treadmill forever.
sents.zh: 它们会让你永远在那台跑步机上跑个不停。

sents.t: Jimmy Carr has this cool idea where he says trajectory is more important than position.
sents.zh: 吉米·卡尔有个很酷的观点，他说趋势比位置更重要。
gloss: 往哪个方向飞的那条线。
你当时站在哪里、处在什么处境

sents.t: So, if you are number one hundred and one in the world, but last year you were number two hundred,
sents.zh: 比如，如果你现在世界排名第一百零一，但去年排第两百，

sents.t: versus you’re number two in the world, but last year you were number one, there is this sense of the deceleration is very, very tangible.
sents.zh: 相比之下，你现在世界第二，但去年是第一，那种下滑的感觉是非常非常真切的。

sents.t: And again it goes back to evolution.
sents.zh: 这又回到了进化。
gloss: 一代代慢慢变出来的样子。

sents.t: Something that is bleeding eventually dies, unless you stop the bleeding, so you’re hardwired not to lose what you have.
sents.zh: 流血的东西最终会死，除非你止住血，所以你天生就不想失去自己拥有的东西。

sents.t: Because we evolved in conditions where we’re so close to just not surviving, you don’t want to give anything up.
sents.zh: 因为我们是在差一点就活不下去的条件下进化来的，所以你什么都不想放弃。
gloss: 慢慢长成了现在的样子。

sents.t: It’s hardwired into us to not give anything up.
sents.zh: 不放弃任何东西，这已经刻在我们骨子里了。
gloss: 线路焊死在里面，改不了。

sents.t: So you grip tightly?
sents.zh: 所以你会紧紧抓住不放？

sents.t: That’s right.
sents.zh: 没错。
